editorial:
Imagine spending your entire summer just a few steps away from Disney World, but you can't actually afford to go inside. You will meet Moonee, a spunky six-year-old who spends her days playing with friends and getting into trouble in a cheap motel. While her world feels like a big playground full of magic and jokes, you can quickly see that the adults around her are just trying to survive. Her mom is doing her best, but she is struggling with money and making some bad choices. It feels like a sunny day that slowly turns into a rainy afternoon, blending the joy of being a kid with the scary reality of being poor.

The acting is what really makes this work, especially since the kids feel like real children and not actors reading a script. The colors are bright and popping, which makes the sad parts hit even harder. You might find the slow pace a bit frustrating at first, but it helps you feel like you are living in that motel too. If you want a story that feels honest and raw, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Things take a sad turn when the state steps in because of the mom's unstable living situation. The police eventually come to take Moonee away from her mother. In the final scene, Moonee doesn't fully understand what is happening, so she runs away from the officers and sprints toward Disney World. She reaches the gates and looks at the magic kingdom, showing that her childhood innocence is gone and her life has changed forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves realistic stories about childhood and family struggles.
